title: Otter AI Pricing for Enterprise Buyers in 2026
summary: Otter AI enterprise pricing reveals the costs for Enterprise versus Business plans. Compare capabilities to decide which tier fits your team's budget.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits Otter buyers run into


Before you accept a quote, check each of three limits against your own usage: monthly transcription minutes, a paid seat for everyone who records, and integrations that only unlock on higher plans. That is where the extra money usually goes.


### Minute and length caps


[31 hours of meetings a month](https://www.petersorgenfrei.com/short-form/83-meetings-are-a-waste-of-time) is what a typical employee sits in, and **Otter Pro allows 20 hours of transcription** .


That leaves 11 hours a month with no transcript, so either a third of that person's meetings go unrecorded or you pay for a higher tier.


Count your meeting hours first. Also check the per-conversation length limit, because a long workshop can stop mid-session.


If three people from one team attend the same call, you're not buying one recorder for the room. Each person who runs the recorder needs their own paid seat.


Count who actually hits record, not who attends. Guests who only read a shared transcript are a separate question, so ask what they can see without a seat.


The cost shows up after you've signed, when the tool you assumed came with your plan doesn't, because connections to calendars, CRMs and task tools can sit on higher plans than the one you priced.


Check export formats and how long transcripts are kept, too. A retention limit means old meetings can disappear when you need them.


### Moving notes into external tools


If a plan's built-in integrations fall short, Activepieces, an automation tool, can route meeting notes into your CRM or task tracker, and its published pricing page states 1 credit per flow run however many steps the flow has, against Zapier's per-task billing and Make's per-module billing on their own pricing pages, with 1,000 credits a month on the free plan.


The version history below shows two saved versions of one such flow, each with a timestamp, so you can go back to the one that worked after a bad edit.


That costs some setup time, but it can be cheaper than moving up a plan.
